requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each testable obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.fingerprints`. I did not request implementation source or the `run_hash` and `node_hash` helpers. I assumed from their names and uses that they return the selected item's structural hash.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**

- **Whitespace-separated words, with word boundaries kept (SHA-256 over the structural encoding):**
  - `tests.rs#fn[prose_words_are_encoded_separately]` asserts that `/// ab cd` and `/// abcd` differ.
  - `tests.rs#fn[string_literals_hash_as_words]` asserts that `"ab cd"` equals `"ab  cd"` and differs from `"abcd"`.
  - `outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` checks the Rust case. Extra spaces keep the fingerprint. `twowords` changes it. The fingerprint is a 64-character hex digest.
  - Nothing checks a known SHA-256 value. That would need the exact encoding, which the text deliberately leaves unspecified. The length and hex-digit assertions are the practical check for the digest.
- **Fingerprint scheme:** the `check` helper in `outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` asserts `Rust.fingerprint_scheme() == "rust-structural-v1"`. It also asserts that loaded content retains the same scheme through `OutlineContent::fingerprint_scheme`.
- **Doc comments participate:**
  - `tests.rs#fn[hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments]` asserts that changing `Doc.` to `Docs.` changes the hash.
  - `tests.rs#fn[editing_a_doc_comment_word_changes_the_hash]` asserts that changing a word changes the hash.
  - `tests.rs#fn[reflowing_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash]` asserts that changing `a b` to `a c`, or reordering it to `b a`, changes the hash.
- **Ordinary comments are excluded:**
  - In `tests.rs#fn[hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments]`, a `// {cite}` line comment whose text changes from `a.b` to `c.d` leaves the hash unchanged.
  - In `outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]`, a `/* note */` block comment changed to `/* edited */` leaves the Rust fingerprint unchanged.
- **Delimiters excluded, and comments of one group hash as one word sequence:**
  - `tests.rs#fn[reflowing_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash]` shows these all hash the same:
    - `/// a` and `/// b` on two lines.
    - `/// a b` on one line.
    - Extra leading and trailing spaces and an empty `///` line.
    - A `/** a\n * b\n */` block with a leading `*`.
  - `tests.rs#fn[reflowing_inner_and_block_doc_comments_keeps_the_hash]` shows these hash the same:
    - `//!` split across lines, and `/*! … */`.
    - `/** … */` and `///`.
- **Inner and outer groups are distinct:** `tests.rs#fn[inner_and_outer_doc_comments_hash_in_separate_groups]` moves a word between a nested item's outer doc comment and the module's inner doc comment. The word sequence is the same either way, yet the hash changes. This test would fail if the two groups were hashed together. The same test also checks that splitting an inner group across comments keeps the hash.
- **Attributes attached to an item participate:** in `tests.rs#fn[hashes_skip_whitespace_and_plain_comments_but_not_doc_comments]`, changing `#[inline]` to `#[cold]` changes the hash. The same test shows that a changed body (`= 1` to `= 2`) changes the hash, and that moving the item or reformatting it across lines leaves it unchanged.
- **Integration level:** `outline_content.rs#fn[rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes]` confirms that:
  - The selected item's span includes its doc comment and attribute.
  - A reformatted item with a reflowed doc comment has the same fingerprint.
  - A changed body has a different fingerprint.

**Remaining questions**

The identity-hash and descendant-exclusion rules belong to `requirements.references.structural_hash`. That requirement is cited here, so I did not reassess it. No acknowledgments were present or needed. I found no requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Documentation comments participate in structural hashes. Ordinary comments
are excluded. Included comment prose is grouped as inner or outer documentation;
delimiters are excluded, and consecutive comments of one group hash as one word
sequence. Reflowing that prose preserves its hash; changing its words changes it.
Attributes attached to an item participate in that item's hash.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
